parsed.explanation: No trans-specific border, facilities or custody regime is documented, and no enforcement frequency for ss.146/148 is sourced, so no universal-exposure tier is established. However the same-sex ban was actively upheld in 2024 with up to 10 years' imprisonment, a 2023 report documents bias-motivated violence and discrimination, cross-dressers were attacked in 2018 and a cross-dressing teenager was assaulted then fraud-prosecuted in 2019, and there is no SOGI legal protection, LGBT organisation or helpline. Thin-data extrapolation from active criminalisation, stigma and absent recourse puts the outcome after outing in the Elevated Risk tier rather than midpoint.

entry_documents.exposure: No visa, entry-screening or document-marker rule affecting trans visitors is sourced.
entry_documents.interaction: Not documented. Foreign passport practice is not described; absence is not evidence of acceptance.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: A cross-dressing teenager was charged with fraud for allegedly pretending to be a woman after assault in 2019; charge withdrawn. No custody-placement practice is sourced.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Presentation can be reframed as deception/fraud, creating investigation risk if outed.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facilities, bathroom, ward or subnational variation law or practice is sourced.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Not documented; no subnational regime is established.

care_services.exposure: No healthcare, medication or HIV-service provision for trans visitors is sourced beyond a regional MSM contact point.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Ss.146 (10 years) and 148 (5 years) criminalise consensual male same-sex conduct; High Court upheld ban 16 Feb 2024. Enforcement frequency not sourced.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No SOGI anti-discrimination or harassment law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Same-sex law is secondary for trans visitors but can act as a state lever via fraud/deception framing, as in 2019.

minors_guardians.exposure: No rule for trans minors or travelling guardians is sourced.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. No LGBT youth helpline or help centre exists.
minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented; minor-specific exposure cannot be inferred from adult cases.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2023 58-page report documents bias-motivated violence and discrimination in daily life. Cross-dressers attacked Sept 2018; teenager assaulted Apr 2019. Incidents are individual cases, not rates.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Head of government condemned 2018 attacks. No functioning trans-specific recourse documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State response was mixed: condemnation in 2018, victim prosecution in 2019.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No organisation dedicated to LGBT people operates; LGBT life described as invisible and stigmatised.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Constitutional challenge failed in 2024, removing the documented legal remedy path for the ban.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-B has routine police stops, confiscation and fines with de facto no remedy. This dossier lacks documented routine stops or entry exclusion, so is not clearly that severe, but shares absent remedy, state deception-framing and bias violence.

0.45-A has routine document-mismatch exposure at checkpoints with detention and humiliation but imprisonment unlikely. Here routine exposure is not documented, yet statutory penalty up to 10 years and documented attacks push it somewhat below 0.45.

0.75-C has passport-marker acceptance, trained respectful inspection, tribunal appeal and compensation. None of those traveller-facing protections is documented here; instead the ban was upheld and no SOGI protection exists, so it rates materially below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: Combined operative regime: no documented universal border/facilities exposure, but outing can interact with an actively upheld criminal ban, fraud-by-presentation prosecution, documented bias violence, and no legal or organisational recourse. The 2019 victim-prosecution shows the state as perpetrator, not only bystander. Stickiness of stigma and thin infrastructure raise everyday risk. Unknown enforcement frequency prevents a lower 0.25-tier rating; documented harms and absent protections prevent Reduced Risk.
